title: Design and implement audit-shipper connector patterns for air-gapped/private deployments with customer-managed storage
creator: Priya Rao
description: Goal: Provide safe, auditable, and configurable forwarding options for audit logs from Redwood Private / VPC / on-prem deployments into customer-managed storage targets. This ticket scopes a set of connector patterns and an implementation plan for the audit shipper (agent and control-plane orchestration), focusing on environments with restricted egress (air-gapped) and enterprise requirements for CMK/HSM encryption, immutability, and retention policies.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Proof-of-concept demonstrates audit events forwarded from a Private deployment into a customer S3 bucket using customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption and server-side validation.
2) Alternative connector for air-gapped customers (file drop via local collector + offline transfer workflow) is documented and tested end-to-end.
3) Uploads are idempotent and provide integrity checks (SHA256) and sequence metadata so downstream SIEMs can reconstruct order.
4) Config options for signed upload mode (presigned URLs/SAS), direct push mode, and pull-proxy mode are available and validated in CI.
5) Design and config have documented threat model and passed security-review checklist.
6) Telemetry surfaces per-bucket success/failure rates and per-event latency in Console dashboards.
tasks: Draft connector patterns document (push, pull, hybrid, offline) and trade-offs
Prototype S3 push with CMK-encrypted multipart uploads and upload-idempotency
Build shipper agent support for generating presigned URLs (S3/GCS/Azure) and fallback to signed-upload daemon
Implement local spool/queue and backpressure semantics for high-throughput tenants
Add integrity header (SHA256) and sequence numbers to audit payloads
Create end-to-end test harness for private deployment using MinIO and Vault KMS
Update Console to accept customer-managed storage config with validation rules
Run security review and hardening (least-privilege IAM doc, token rotation, ephemeral creds)
Write runbook for onboarding and for recovery when uploads fail
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Product and Security. Agreed to prioritize three connector modes: direct push to CMK-backed object stores, presigned URL push, and air-gap compatible local spool + offline transfer. PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUD/Shielded+Audit+Connectors

2026-03-04: Prototype: agent can sign and upload 10MB blobs to S3 using customer CMK; tested server-side encryption:aws:kms and SSE-C flows. Notes: SSE-C increases exposure of key material locally; flagged in security review draft.

2026-03-08: Implemented local spool with disk-backed queue and idempotency keys. Verified recovery after agent restart retains order for in-flight batches. Found case where multipart upload retries could create duplicate parts; added upload-id dedup metadata and manifest file per upload.

2026-03-12: Security review initial pass completed. Team recommended removing SSE-C from default flow, require envelope encryption with customer CMK or client-side encryption done by customer. Action item: document HSM/KMS integration patterns and rotation recommendations.
review_comments: PM (Aisha Gupta): Ensure onboarding UX in Console validates customer bucket policies and VPC endpoint configurations before accepting config.

Security (Elliot Chen): Avoid storing long-lived plaintext keys on host; use short-lived STS credentials and rotate every 1h by default. Consider signed-upload broker to keep Redwood control plane out of key custody for hosted-managed scenarios.
Design (Maya Lin): Recommend adding a visual flow in Console explaining push vs pull trade-offs for non-engineer admins.
Infra (Benji Cole): For on-prem MinIO/Ceph targets, test AWS v4 signing compatibility and path-style vs virtual-host buckets; add integration tests.
Legal: Confirm retention and immutability features align with customer contractual SLAs; provide opt-in WORM guidance.
decisions: Adopt three primary connector modes: direct push (agent->customer-store using customer creds), presigned (control-plane provides presigned URLs which agent uses to upload without custody of keys), and local-spool offline (for air-gapped environments where customer will pull files).

Default to envelope encryption using customer-managed KMS (CMK) where possible. Explicitly deprecate SSE-C as a Redwood default due to key custody concerns; allow only with explicit customer acceptance documented in onboarding.
Implement idempotency and SHA256 integrity headers for all uploads; require sequence metadata to allow downstream ordering checks.
Telemetry and observability: agent exposes per-batch metrics; Console surfaces upload success rates and last-success timestamp per destination.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Push mode (direct) offers lowest end-to-end latency but requires Redwood agent to hold or assume credentials; increases blast radius if misconfigured. Mitigation: short-lived STS, least-privilege IAM roles, and optional isolation mode where agent can only write to a specific prefix.

Presigned mode reduces credential exposure but requires a reliable control-plane->agent channel or periodic refresh; risk of presigned URL leakage if not rotated. Mitigation: short TTL (minutes) and one-time use IDs.

Air-gap/local-spool mode minimizes external connectivity needs but increases operational burden on customer (manual transfer or scheduled pull). Risk of lost events if local disk is exhausted; mitigation: retention throttle, disk-usage alerts, and optional remote replication appliances.
Customer-managed KMS integration introduces operational complexity across cloud vendors; enforcement of correct key policies and IAM docs required.
implementation_notes: Agent component: shipper-daemon will run as a containerized DaemonSet on customer clusters and as a system service for on-prem VMs. It exposes a control socket for graceful drain/rotate.
Upload protocol: support AWS S3 multipart uploads with upload manifest JSON containing sequence ranges and SHA256 digests; support GCS resumable uploads and Azure block blobs via SAS tokens.

Fallbacks: Agent should retry with exponential backoff and snapshot failed batches to /var/lib/redwood/audit_spool for manual retrieval. Provide a CLI tool 'redwood-audit-tool' to replay spooled batches.
Validation: Console config flow will run a dry-run validation (attempt presigned URL handshake or STS assume-role test). Failure modes surfaced with actionable remediation steps.
test_plan:
1) Integration: Deploy Private with a MinIO instance configured as customer-managed storage; run synthetic traffic at 500 req/s for 30m and assert 100% delivery to bucket, correct SHA256 metadata, and retained ordering.
2) End-to-end: Validate presigned flow by having control-plane generate presigned URLs and agent upload without holding keys. Verify URLs expire and one-time-use semantics.
3) Failure modes: simulate disk-full and network blackhole; verify agent queues, raises alerts, and recovers without data loss when storage restored.
4) Security: Key rotation test where CMK policy rotates weekly; confirm agent uploads remain accepted and old manifests are still verifiable.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal E2E with MinIO and Vault KMS (approx 2 sprints). Phase 2: Beta with 2 enterprise customers on Private deployment, support presigned and direct push. Phase 3: General availability with Console onboarding wizard and runbook. Monitor for errors and if >1% failure rate across customers, rollback direct-push default and force presigned mode.
runbook_snippets: - On upload failures: check agent logs (/var/log/redwood/shipper.log) for 4xx/5xx. If 403 from S3, validate IAM role and prefix. - On disk pressure: stop other non-essential pods, run 'redwood-audit-tool replay' after freeing space. - Key rotation mismatch: validate envelope metadata and re-encrypt manifests using customer's rotation tool.
notes_for_oncall: Alert 'audit_shipper_upload_fails' should fire when 5xx rate exceeds 0.5% for 5m. On-call should contact customer success for affected tenants and initiate replay flow if necessary.
next_steps: Complete implementation of presigned URL broker (control-plane) and add CI integration tests for AWS/GCP/Azure. Schedule security-review follow-up the week after phase 1 completion.
